procnotices.bid_description: Procurement Officer for Bulsho Project-Somaliland Project Implementation Unit (PIU)
procnotices.contact_address: Near the Presidential Palace, behind the Ministry of Livestock, Hargeisa, Somaliland.
procnotices.contact_organization: Ministry of Local Governments and Urban Development
procnotices.notice_text:
GOVERNMENT OF SOMALILAND

MINISTRY OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT (MoLGUD)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

Country: Somaliland
Project ID: P508408
Project Name: Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience
Consulting Service: PIU Bulsho Procurement Officer
Selection Type: Individual Consultant

Reference No: SO-MOLGUD-567779-CS-INDV
Duty Station: Hargeisa, Somaliland, with potential travel to the target districts and cities of the Bulsho Project
Duration: 12 months, renewable subject to satisfactory performance
Application Deadline: September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Hargeisa Time

1. BACKGROUND

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD) of the Government of Somaliland is implementing the World Bank-financed Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408).

The main objective of the Bulsho Program is to strengthen community and local institutions for improved social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. The Program places citizens and communities at the center of governance and focuses on strengthening service delivery systems, reinforcing the social contract between citizens and government, and promoting participatory and inclusive local governance.

To support implementation of the Bulsho Project, the Government of Somaliland, through MoLGUD, intends to recruit a qualified and experienced Procurement Officer as part of the Project Implementation Unit (PIU).

2. SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The PIU Bulsho Procurement Officer will be responsible for developing and implementing an effective and cost-efficient procurement management system for the Bulsho Project in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations, applicable Government procedures, the Project Operations Manual (POM), and other relevant project requirements.

The Procurement Officer will coordinate and support procurement planning and implementation; preparation and processing of procurement documents; bid/proposal evaluation and contract award processes; contract management; procurement compliance, monitoring and reporting; community-level procurement; procurement capacity building; and maintenance of procurement records and systems, including the Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP).

The detailed scope of services, responsibilities, deliverables, reporting arrangements, and other requirements are provided in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR).

3. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The successful candidate shall meet the following minimum qualifications and experience:

  • A university degree from an accredited university in Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, or an equivalent relevant discipline.
  • A minimum of six (6) years of directly relevant professional experience, including broad experience in the management of procurement in the public or private sector.
  • A minimum of four (4) years of experience implementing procurement activities in accordance with the procurement guidelines and procedures of international organizations, such as the World Bank, African Development Bank, United Nations, INGOs, or similar development partners, particularly in the procurement of goods and services.
  • Demonstrated interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in a team environment.
  • Knowledge and understanding of project planning and implementation.
  • High standards of reliability, integrity, ethical conduct, and professional accountability.
  • Strong communication and representation skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively in multicultural and challenging environments.
  • Excellent computer skills, particularly in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and internet-based applications.
  • Knowledge of Somaliland’s public financial management laws and regulations.
  • Knowledge of World Bank and/or other development partner procurement standards and requirements.
  • Strong working knowledge of written and spoken English.

 

4. REPORTING AND DURATION

The PIU Bulsho Procurement Officer will report to the Bulsho Project Manager.

The assignment will initially be for 12 months and may be renewed subject to satisfactory performance and project requirements. The duty station is Hargeisa, Somaliland, with potential travel to the target districts and cities of the Bulsho Project.

5. SELECTION METHOD

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD), Government of Somaliland, now invites eligible and qualified Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing – Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations and applicable Government of Somaliland policies.

6. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Interested Consultants should submit:

  1. A detailed and updated Curriculum Vitae (CV), including contact details of three (3) professional referees;
  2. Copies of relevant academic qualification certificates; and
  3. A cover letter outlining the candidate’s relevant experience, qualifications, and suitability for the assignment.

Interested and qualified candidates should submit their applications by email with the subject line:

“Application for PIU Bulsho Procurement Officer – SO-MOLGUD-567779-CS-INDV”

To: bulsho.somaliland@outlook.com
Cc: dg.molgud@sldgov.org

Applications must be received no later than September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Hargeisa Time.

Attention:

PIU Bulsho Procurement Officer Recruitment
Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience
Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD)
Government of Somaliland
Hargeisa, Somaliland

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this REOI.

procnotices.notice_text:
BALOCHISTAN WATER SECURITY AND PRODUCTIVITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR THE SELECTION OF SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT SPECIALIST / INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT

            The Government of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, through the Government of Balochistan (GoB), with support of the World Bank (WB), is implementing the Balochistan Water Security and Productivity Improvement Project (BWSPIP). The project development objective is to improve flood protection, increase access to water for productive use, and improve water supply service delivery in selected areas of Balochistan. It intends to apply part of the funds to cover eligible payments to hire the services of motivated, experienced, and energetic individual to work with the Project Implementation Unit as SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT SPECIALIST / Individual Consultant.                       

S.No

Position

Qualification/Experience

1.

SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT SPECIALIST

  • Master’s degree (minimum 16 years of education) specifically in Sociology, Social Sciences, Rural Development, Community Development, Development Studies from a recognized university.
  • Minimum seven (07) years of post-qualification professional experience in social development, social safeguards management, stakeholder engagement, community development, or social risk management, preferably in urban water supply and sanitation, municipal services, utility strengthening and infrastructure development.
  • Demonstrated experience in the development sector, preferably in projects related to urban water supply and sanitation, institutional strengthening, public service delivery, or community development.
  • Proven experience in stakeholder engagement, training and awareness raising, and community consultation processes involving project-affected communities, water consumers, residents of low-income and underserved areas, community-based organizations, vulnerable groups and conflict-sensitive engagement approaches.
  • Demonstrated experience in design, management, and monitoring of grievance redressal mechanisms (GRM) and social risk mitigation measures. (Certifications required)
  • Experience working in similar geographical and socio-cultural conditions, particularly in urban, peri-urban, underserved, and vulnerable communities. Familiarity with the institutional arrangements, local governance systems, socio-economic conditions, and community dynamics of Quetta will be an added advantage.
  • Strong communication, coordination, documentation, and reporting skills.
  • Knowledge of local languages.

 

The Government of Balochistan, represented by the Project Director, PIU-BWSPIP (Component-B), now invites eligible individuals to indicate their interest in providing the services.  Interested consultants must provide detailed CVs describing that they are qualified to perform the services as per the criteria defined in the document titled “Terms of Reference”, which can be downloaded from the project website by following the link http://www.bwspip-b.org.pk.

Eligible candidates who meet the required criteria are encouraged to submit their EOI/CV, along with a cover letter, by 04th September 2026 via email at procurement.bwspip.qwasa@gmail.com. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToRs) are available at https://bwspip-b.org.pk/.

 

Important Note:

  • The CV submitted by applicants must clearly demonstrate and cross-reference the candidate’s experience against the specific scope of services and responsibilities provided in these TORs. Generic or unrelated experience will not be considered sufficient.
  • It should be ensured that only the contact details of professional references are required, and not the contact details of all previous employers.
  • Any misleading information will result in disqualification of candidate.

 

The Individual Consultant shall be selected in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Procurement in Investment Project Financing – Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services (Fifth Edition, September 2023), under the Selection of Individual Consultants method.

procnotices.notice_text:
Recurrent Cost and Reform Financing Project (RCRFP III)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI) (CONSULTING SERVICES) FIRMS SELECTION

COUNTRY:                           Federal Republic of Somalia (FGS)

NAME OF PROJECT          Somalia Recurrent Cost & Reform Financing (RCRF) Project - Phase III                                  

PROJECT ID                          P173731

Grant No.                            IDA-E3120

Assignment Title: Special Audit of Payroll Data Migration and Integrity in Somalia Federal Member States. Reference No: SO-MOF-564851-CS-CQS

Place of assignment:  Mogadishu and other Federal Member States of Somalia

Background

I. The Federal Government of Somalia, through the Ministry of Finance has received financing from the World Bank for the Somalia Recurrent Cost and Reform Financing Project that supports the FGS and eligible Federal Member States (FMS) in strengthening resource management systems, the intergovernmental fiscal relations, and service delivery in health and education. The project disburses financing against Performance-Based Conditions (PBCs), under which payment follows independently verified evidence that agreed reform milestones have been achieved, rather than against inputs alone. The objective of the audit is to provide reasonable assurance on payroll migration completeness, legitimacy of payroll entries, authorized payment execution, and resolution of material control weaknesses.

II. The Government intends to apply part of the proceeds in the Procurement of Consulting Special Audit of Payroll Data Migration and Integrity in Somalia Federal Member States

III. The Ministry of Finance now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.  

The short-listing criteria are as follows:

A. Core business and years in business: The firm must be a registered, audit or professional services firm, affiliated with an institute that is a full member of the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) with a core business focus on financial and auditing. The firm must have been in operation for ten (10) years.

B. Relevant Experience: The firm should demonstrate experience in financial auditing, public financial management, HR, or governance, with successful execution of at least two (2) similar assignments. For each referenced assignment, provide evidence related to the assignment, including title, scope of work, client name, address, and contact details, duration, and contract value.

C. Technical and managerial capacity: The firm should demonstrate sufficient technical and managerial capacity to carry out the assignment.; and

D. The technical and managerial capability of the firm. (Provide  the structure of the organization, general qualifications, and the number of key staff, thier CVs and their qualifications.

IV. Terms of Reference:

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found at the following website: www.mof.gov.so  or it can be forwarded to the applicant upon submission of the application to the address indicated below.

V. Selection Method:

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14, 3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" July 2016, revised November 2017 revised August 2018, November 2020, 2023 and 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and eligibility.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Interested Consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours from 8:30 am to 3.30 pm Mogadishu time (Excluding public holidays).

Expressions of interest (EOI) should be delivered by e-mail below indicating “SO-MOF-564851-CS-CQS Procurement of Consulting Special Audit of Payroll Data Migration and Integrity in Somalia Federal Member States); on the email subject to the address below by  2nd  September 2026 at 12:00 Hours (Mogadishu Time)2026 at 12:00 Hours (Mogadishu Time)

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Productive Safety Net program VI and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for e-payment service for Cluster of Tigray and Afar regions.

 

  1. The Food Security Coordination Office of the Ministry of Agriculture now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for: e-payment service for Cluster of Tigray and Afar regions.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Republic of Armenia

Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Project (TRIP)

Loan No: IBRD-98090

Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for project performance Monitoring & Evaluation

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): TRIP-CS-01

17 August, 2026

The Republic of Armenia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Project (TRIP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include supporting ATDF in establishing and implementing a practical and reliable Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) system for the Project, enabling systematic tracking of project implementation progress, measurement of results and outcomes, and timely reporting against the Project Results Framework.

Specifically, the Consultant will:

  • Operationalize the existing Results Framework (presented in Annex 1);
  • Update and validate baseline data where needed;
  • Develop and implement a fit-for-purpose M&E methodology;
  • Conduct data collection, analysis, and reporting;

The anticipated date of contract signing is May 2027. The expected completion date of the assignment August, 2030.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

 

The Armenian Territorial Development Fund (ATDF) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

(Experience during the last five (5) years)

  • Experience in the development, implementation and/or operation of Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) systems.
  • Experience in planning and conducting baseline and status quo assessments, socio-economic and/or tourism sector studies, including data collection, analysis, and preparation of analytical reports.
  • Experience in designing and implementing quantitative and qualitative research, including survey design, sampling methodologies, and data analysis.
  • Experience in conducting similar studies in the regions (marzes) of the Republic of Armenia.
  • Experience in developing and/or implementing digital monitoring platforms (M&E databases/dashboards) or digital results management tools under at least one (1) project.

* The Consultant shall provide information on contracts completed by the firm, including the name of the Client, contract value, and a brief description of the services provided.

 Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The shortlist will contain five (5) to eight (8) firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 09:00 to 17:00 (Yerevan time).

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by August 31, 2026.

Armenian Territorial Development Fund

Procurement department

K. Ulnetsi st. 31bld

Yerevan 0037, Armenia

Tel: (+374 60) 50-15-60 +140

E-mail: procurementatdf2026@gmail.com, m.grigoryan@atdf.am

 

 

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Project

Consultancy Service for

PROJECT PERFORMANCE MONITORING & EVALUATION

TRIP-CS-01

The Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Project (Project) aims to boost Armenia's tourism potential through targeted infrastructure and soft investments in several regions. It will support seven (Areni, Yeghegis, Jermuk, Dvin, Gyumri, Dilijan, Goris) of the twenty identified tourism clusters, focusing on wine, wellness, adventure, culture, education, and ecotourism across Ararat, Vayots Dzor, Shirak, Aragatsotn Tavush, and Syunik regions. The Project will improve connectivity to the Clusters and enhance tourism site infrastructure. It also seeks to elevate Armenia’s natural assets and human resources, improving business and professional skills in nearby communities to maximize the job creation. Additionally, Project aligns with the World Bank’s approach to attracting private investment in these tourism clusters.

Project development objective (PDO) is to improve access to climate-resilient infrastructure and increase tourism contribution to the local economy of project-supported clusters in Armenia.

Section 2. Objective of the assignment

The objective of this assignment is to support ATDF in establishing and implementing a practical and reliable Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) system for the Project, enabling systematic tracking of project implementation progress, measurement of results and outcomes, and timely reporting against the Project Results Framework.

Specifically, the Consultant will:

  • Operationalize the existing Results Framework (presented in Annex 1);
  • Update and validate baseline data where needed;
  • Develop and implement a fit-for-purpose M&E methodology;
  • Conduct data collection, analysis, and reporting;

Section 3. Scope of Work

Task 1: Operationalization of Existing M&E Framework (Status Update)

The Consultant shall:

  • Review existing Results Framework, M&E arrangements, indicators, and reporting practices developed under the previous Project (Local Economy and Infrastructure Development Project) and propose changes in the methodology for TRIP.;
  • Update and validate baseline data using available sources;
  • Develop and document proposed measurement approaches for each indicator, including data sources, collection methods, frequency, responsibilities, and data verification procedures;
  • Provide recommendations to strengthen the operationalization and implementation of the Project M&E system, including measures to improve data quality, consistency, and reporting.

Task 2: Status quo analysis.

Prior to Implementation of the Civil works in the target locations the Consultant shall analyze and assess the number of visitors to a given site (subproject) through analyzing formal visitations (e.g. tickets, etc.), hotels, B&Bs, etc. of 2023-2026 years, and other informal means, as well as some qualitative assessment, e.g. view of the quality of infrastructure, site offerings, etc. Consultant shall also:

  • Establish baseline values for all PDO and Intermediate Results indicators;
  • Develop indicator measurement protocols, including calculation formulas, data sources, verification procedures, treatment of missing data, and responsibilities for data collection and validation;
  • Conduct mapping and profiling of tourism-related enterprises and tourism value-chain actors in project-supported clusters.

Task 3: M&E Methodology and Development

The Consultant shall develop a practical and implementable M&E methodology, including:

  • Indicator reference sheets (definitions, data sources, data disaggregation;
  • Data collection methods and sources (surveys, administrative data, other secondary sources);
  • Surveys methodologies, including data collection tools and sampling approach (proportionate and feasible);
  • Data quality assurance procedures, including identification of limitations related to data availability, response rate, attribution of results, and seasonal variability, and proposed mitigation measures
  • Description of the organization and implementation of the field works;
  • Data management and storage protocols;
  • Reporting templates (quarterly, annual, final).

The M&E Methodology should include a data collection calendar that allows for counting seasonality, provides guidelines for interviewers on how to conduct surveys in the field and develops survey instruments that are in line with international standards. It also should specify data imputation, parameter estimation methodologies and determine the structure of periodic Results Reports.

M&E Methodology should be based on all selected regions, a parallel analysis of the project’s impacts in the context of tourism development throughout Armenia would be of special interest; in particular, analysis of historical trends (before, during and after the project) of specific tourism indicators at the national level and for different regions.

Task 3: Pilot Testing and Initial Implementation

The Consultant shall:

  • Design and pilot data collection tools (e.g., visitor surveys, business surveys);
  • Conduct pilot data collection in selected clusters;
  • Refine tools and methodology based on pilot results;
  • Support initial round of data collection.

Task 4: Design and Development of a Digital M&E System

The Consultant shall:

  • Design and develop a digital M&E database and indicator tracking solution to support systematic collection, storage, management, and monitoring of project results;
  • Develop an interactive dashboard solution (preferably Power BI or equivalent) for tracking, analysis, visualization, and reporting of Project Results Framework indicators, including disaggregation and progress against targets, where applicable; Develop database architecture, data entry templates, user roles, access protocols, and data management procedures to support the long-term operation and sustainability of the M&E system;
  • Prepare user guidance materials, operating procedures, and technical documentation for the database and dashboard solution;
  • Prepare training and capacity building plan and deliver training and capacity-building sessions for ATDF designated project staff on the use, administration, maintenance, and updating of the M&E database and dashboard tools;
  • Support pilot operation, testing, and refinement of the digital M&E system prior to its final handover.

Task 5: Reporting and Results Assessment

The Consultant shall:

  • Produce periodic M&E reports (quarterly and annual);
  • Analyze progress toward PDO and Intermediate Results indicators, identify trends, implementation challenges, and emerging risks;
  • Prepare a Final Results Report.

Section 4. Deliverables

The Consultant shall deliver the following outputs. All deliverables shall be submitted in English and Armenian, in electronic (editable MS Word/Excel formats), and, where required, two (2) hard copies.

4.1. Inception Report (Month 1)

Indicative length: 15–20 pages

Content:

  • Detailed work plan and implementation schedule (Gantt chart);
  • Refined understanding of assignment objectives and scope;
  • Proposed M&E methodological approach (high-level);
  • Mapping of available data sources and stakeholders;
  • Risks, assumptions, and mitigation measures;
  • Detailed structure of all subsequent deliverables;

Annexes:

  • Draft survey tools (visitor, business, beneficiary);
  • Draft indicator reference sheet template;

4.2. Status Update Report (Month 2)

Indicative length: 20 pages

Content:

  • Review of existing indicators and definitions;
  • Updated/validated baseline values (based on available data);
  • Identification of data gaps, inconsistencies, and limitations;

4.3. Status Quo Analysis Report (For each Cluster prior to the commencement of construction works)

Indicative length: 30–50 pages

Content:

  • Review of baseline information available in the approved Cluster Development Plans (CDPs), feasibility studies, design documentation, official statistics, and other relevant sources supporting the Project Results Framework;
  • Assessment of visitor numbers and tourism flows for the period 2023–2026 using available administrative, statistical, and other relevant data sources;
  • Collection of additional baseline information only where existing data are insufficient to establish baseline values or measure the indicators included in the approved Project Results Framework;
  • Compilation of baseline values for PDO and Intermediate Results indicators in accordance with the approved Results Framework;
  • Identification of data gaps, limitations, and recommendations for future data collection and monitoring;
  • Preparation of baseline datasets and supporting documentation for subsequent project monitoring.

Outputs:

• Status Quo Analysis Report for each target location/subproject;
• Baseline dataset and supporting data tables.
 

4.4. M&E Methodology and Toolkit (Month 8)

Indicative length: 30–50 pages

Content:

  • Indicator Reference Sheets (definition, unit, baseline, target, data source);
  • Indicator Measurement Protocols for all PDO and Intermediate Results indicators;
  • Outcome and impact assessment methodology.
  • Data collection methodologies:
  • Surveys (visitor, enterprise, beneficiary)
  • Administrative and secondary data;
  • Sampling approach;
  • Data quality assurance and validation procedures;
  • Data management and storage protocols, including ethical standards and data privacy protection procedures;
  • Reporting framework and standardized templates;
  • Data collection calendar (including seasonality considerations).

Mandatory Annexes:

  • Survey questionnaires;
  • Data entry and database templates (Excel or compatible);
  • Reporting templates (quarterly, annual).

4.5. Pilot Testing and Initial Implementation Report (Month 8)

Indicative length: 30–50 pages

Content:

  • Description of pilot implementation (locations, sample size, tools used);
  • Results of pilot data collection;
  • Identified methodological and operational issues;
  • Adjustments made to tools and methodology;
  • Finalized data collection instruments and procedures;

Outputs:

  • Revised/final survey instruments and data collection protocols;

4.6. Digital M&E System and Dashboard Package (Month 6)

 

Outputs

  • Operational digital M&E database;
  • Interactive dashboard with user access levels;
  • Data entry manual;
  • System administration manual;
  • Training plan and training materials;
  • Training sessions based on the agreed training plan.

4.7. Periodic M&E Reports (Quarterly and Annual)

Indicative length: 30–50 pages

Content:

  • Progress against intermediate indicators;
  • Analysis of trends and performance;
  • Key findings and interpretation of results;
  • Identification of implementation challenges and risks;
  • Recommendations for corrective actions;

Format requirements:

  • Executive summary (max. 2–3 pages);
  • Main analytical narrative;
  • Visualizations (charts, graphs, tables);

4.8. Final Results Report (End of Assignment)

Indicative length: up to 80–100 pages

 

Content:

  • Overall assessment of project performance against PDO;
  • Consolidated analysis of all indicators over time;
  • Assessment of project contribution to tourism development;
  • Economic analysis;
  • Lessons learned and good practices;
  • Strategic recommendations for future tourism sector monitoring and similar projects implementation;

Annexes:

  • Indicator time-series tables;
  • Methodological notes.

 

Section 5. The composition of Consultant’s team and qualifications are the following:

Key 1 Team Leader: hold Master’s degree with an emphasis on tourism research, monitoring and evaluation, with at least 5-7 years of similar experience in survey design and execution;

Key 2 Economic and financial analysis expert: Bachelor’s degree in Economics, Mathematics, Social Sciences or related field with at least 5 years of experience in data collection and analysis.

Key 3 Performance evaluation specialist: Bachelor degree in tourism with at least 5 years of experience in data collection and analysis for tourism development. Willing to travel to remote  communities and coordinate with team members on related projects;

Key 4 Qualified Surveyors in related field with at least 3 years’ experience in similar M&E assignments /4 specialist/.

 

Section 6. Language

The working language of the report is English and Armenian. All reports should be submitted in hard (2) and electronic copies in both languages.

Section 7. Duration

The Contract shall be signed for an initial period of one (1) year. The Consultant shall be responsible for addressing the Client’s comments and finalizing the deliverables until their formal acceptance by the Client. The Contract may be renewed annually, subject to satisfactory performance and the continuing needs of the Project.

Section 8. Implementation Arrangements

The Consultant shall report directly to the ATDF. Close coordination will be required with Tourism Committee, National Statistical Committee (upon need), and other relevant stakeholders. Close coordination with ATDF technical team and construction contractors will also be required. The assignment is on an intermittent basis following the pace of the progress of civil works implementation in each of the selected regions.

REPÚBLICA DEL PERÚ

PROGRAMA DE INVERSIÓN PARA EL MEJORAMIENTO DE LA GESTIÓN DE TRÁNSITO Y APOYO AL TRANSPORTE SOSTENIBLE EN LIMA METROPOLITANA

TRANSPORTE URBANO Y MOVILIDAD URBANA

ANUNCIO GENERAL DE ADQUISICIONES

Préstamo N° 9733-EF

 

La República del Perú ha recibido un préstamo del Banco Internacional de Reconstrucción y Fomento (BIRF) por un monto equivalente a US$ 150 000 000,00 (Ciento Cincuenta Millones y 00/100 dólares americanos), y se propone utilizar los fondos para efectuar los pagos correspondientes a la adquisición de bienes y la contratación de obras, los servicios conexos y los servicios de consultoría en el marco de este proyecto; asimismo, este proyecto contará con la contribución de una contrapartida por la Municipalidad Metropolitana de Lima. El Proyecto es ejecutado por la Municipalidad Metropolitana de Lima, en calidad de entidad ejecutora, a través del Proyecto Especial para la Gestión del Tránsito en Lima Metropolitana (PROTRÁNSITO) y su Unidad de Coordinación Técnica.

El Proyecto financiará obras de adecuación vial y urbana, canalización y tendido de fibra óptica, instalación de infraestructura semafórica, mejoramiento de intersecciones, zonas de tráfico calmado y vías para ciclistas. Asimismo, comprenderá la adquisición e instalación de semáforos, controladores, cámaras, sensores, servidores, equipos de comunicación y seguridad, mobiliario, software y plataformas de gestión del tránsito y detección de infracciones. También se contratarán servicios de diseño, integración tecnológica, pruebas, puesta en funcionamiento, capacitación, supervisión, gestión del Programa y asistencia técnica especializada.

El proyecto comprenderá los siguientes componentes:

  • Componente 1: Sistema de Semáforos
    • Subcomponente 1.1 Red de Semáforos Centralizados.
    • Subcomponente 1.2 Centro de Control de Tránsito.
  • Componente 2: Sistema Automatizado de Detección de Infracciones de Tránsito.
    • Subcomponente 2.1 Centro de Detección y Control de Infracciones de Tránsito e Intersecciones
  • Componente 3: Intersecciones y Barrios Seguros.
    • Subcomponente 3.1 Plan de Acciones Inmediatas de Tránsito (PAIT)
    • Subcomponente 3.2 Zonas de tráfico calmado – Supermanzanas (ZTC)
  • Componente 4: Ciclo-Infraestructura y Calles Completas.
    • Subcomponente 4.1 Infraestructura de Transporte Cicloviario
  • Componente 5: Gestión del Programa y Desarrollo de Capacidades.
    • Subcomponente 5.1 Gestión Técnica y Administrativa del programa
    • Subcomponente 5.2 Gestión Ambiental y Social. Estrategias Sectoriales

 

La adquisición de contratos financiados por el Banco Mundial se llevará a cabo mediante los procedimientos establecidos en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión, Adquisiciones en Operaciones de Financiamiento para Proyectos de Inversión: Bienes, Obras, Servicios de No-Consultoría y Servicios de Consultoría del Banco Mundial (setiembre de 2023) (las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), y estará abierta a todas las empresas y personas elegibles, según se define en dichas Regulaciones. El Banco Mundial dispondrá la publicación, en su sitio web externo, del Plan de Adquisiciones inicial acordado y de todas sus actualizaciones posteriores, una vez que haya otorgado su no objeción.

Los avisos específicos de adquisiciones correspondientes a contratos sujetos a procedimientos competitivos internacionales abiertos se publicarán, conforme estén disponibles, en el sitio web externo del Banco Mundial y en la página web de la Municipalidad Metropolitana de Lima https://www.munlima.gob.pe/ y/o diarios de circulación nacional del país del Prestatario.

RÉPUBLIQUE DU BURUNDI

MINISTERE DES FINANCES, DU BUDGET ET DE L’ECONOMIE NUMERIQUE

PROJET D’APPUI AUX FONDATIONS DE L’ECONOMIE NUMERIQUE AU BURUNDI « PAFEN »

Pays : Burundi

N° du projet : P 17 63 96/P 18 09 87

Don N° : E0930-BI/E2820-BI

Réf : N° BI-PAFEN-PIU-2.4.5.10-CS-INDV

Emis le : 17 Août 2026

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

(Services de consultant individuel)

 

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT CHARGE DE L’ASSURANCE QUALITÉ DANS LE CADRE DE L’ACQUISITION D’UNE PLATEFORME ELECTRONIQUE DE GESTION DES MARCHES PUBLICS ÉLECTRONIQUES (e-GP) AU BURUNDI

  1. Le Gouvernement du Burundi a obtenu un don de la Banque mondiale (BM) pour financer le Projet d’Appui aux Fondations de l’Economie Numérique (PAFEN) d'un montant total de 92 millions de dollars américains, y compris le financement additionnel pour la modernisation de la gestion des finances publiques (GFP).
  2. Il est prévu qu'une partie des ressources de ce projet, spécialement de ce financement additionnel dédié à la « Modernisation de la gestion des finances publiques (GEP) », soit utilisée pour financer les prestations « d’un consultant charge de l’assurance qualité dans le cadre de l’acquisition d’une plateforme électronique de gestion des marches publics (e-GP) ».
  3. Le PAFEN désire recruter, un consultant charge de l’assurance- qualité dans le cadre de l’acquisition d’une plateforme électronique de gestion des marches publics (e-GP) ».
  4. La mission du consultant consiste à assurer la mise en œuvre effective de la fonction assurance qualité dans le cadre du développement, du déploiement et de l’exploitation du système électronique de gestion des marchés publics (e-GP).
  5. Plus spécifiquement, le Consultant aura pour missions de :
  • Élaborer un plan d’assurance qualité (PAQ) précisant les méthodes, outils, critères de validation, modalités de suivi et responsabilités liés à la qualité du projet, en cohérence avec les standards internationaux et les pratiques recommandées par la Banque mondiale ;
  • Vérifier et garantir la conformité des livrables aux spécifications techniques et fonctionnelles du projet détaillées dans le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres ;
  • Proposer des mécanismes de suivi qualité permettant de garantir que les processus de développement, de test et de déploiement respectent les normes de qualité applicables, les bonnes pratiques en matière d’ingénierie logicielle et les délais contractuels, en identifiant les écarts éventuels et en recommandant des actions correctives ;
  • Formuler des recommandations techniques et fonctionnelles pour améliorer les performances de la plateforme e-GP, sa sécurité, son ergonomie et sa convivialité, Cela doit être basé sur les retours des utilisateurs, des exigences d’accessibilité (comme WCAG 2.1) et des bonnes pratiques internationales en matière d’expérience utilisateur(UX) ;
  • Identifier de manière proactive les risques liés à la qualité, tels que les défauts de performance, d’accessibilité, de sécurité ou d’intégration, et proposer des mesures correctives ou préventive

6. Le projet PAFEN invite les candidats intéressés, à manifester leur intérêt pour fournir les services attendus dans le cadre de la présente mission de consultant et à fournir des renseignements démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications et l'expérience pertinentes requises pour exécuter les Services

7. Durée et conditions de la mission

La mission est estimée à une charge de -100 homme-jours effectifs, à répartir selon l’avancement réel des travaux du prestataire chargé du développement de la solution e-GP.

Plutôt que d’intervenir de manière continue, le consultant sera mobilisé de façon séquencée, en fonction des étapes clés du projet (revu technique, validation de livrables, phases de tests, etc.), conformément au calendrier d’exécution du projet et en coordination avec l’ARMP et le Responsable de la digitalisation des marchés publics.

8. Qualifications et expérience requises

Les qualifications requises pour le consultant chargé de l’assurance qualité sont les suivantes :

  • Avoir un master (ou un BAC+5) en Technologies de l’Information et de la Communication spécialité Génie logicielle ou équivalente ;
  • Avoir au moins sept (7) ans d’expérience dans l’assurance qualité de projets informatiques, avoir cette expérience dans le domaine des plateformes e-GP ou de gestion des finances publiques constituant un atout ;
  • Avoir réalisé au moins deux (2) missions d’assurance qualité pour un système d’information d’envergure nationale pour le compte d’une institution publique ;
  • Justifier d’une maîtrise approfondie des normes internationales et des bonnes pratiques relatives aux marchés publics électroniques (e-GP), démontrée au travers d’études de cas issues de réalisations antérieures ou de publications scientifiques.
  • Justifier d’une maîtrise avérée des méthodologies et référentiels d’assurance qualité (notamment ISTQB, TMMi, ISO/IEC 25010) et des principes du développement agile (tels que Scrum, Kanban). La détention de certifications pertinentes représente un atout significatif.
  • Avoir une expérience dans la maitrise des outils d’identification des bugs et conduite de tests sur les systèmes d’informations tels que JIRA, Bugzilla, TestRail, Selenium, JUnit, TestNG, Cypress, etc.
  • Compétences linguistiques : maîtrise écrite et orale du français et de l’anglais.

Toutes ces qualifications et compétences doivent être supportées par des attestations ou des certificats y relatifs.

9. Informations complémentaires (Termes de Références de la mission)

Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse ci-dessous du lundi à vendredi de 8 h : 00 à 12 h : 00 et de 14h :00 à 17h :00 (heures locales : GMT+2).

Les Termes de Références (TDRs) détaillés de la mission peuvent être consultés/téléchargés sur le site web du PAFEN (https://pafen.gov.bi/)  ou retirés au secrétariat du PAFEN à l’adresse ci-dessous.

10. Dépôt des manifestations d’intérêt

Les manifestations d'intérêt doivent être livrées par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous (en personne, ou par courrier, ou par e-mail) avant le 02 Septembre 2026 au plus tard à 17 heures heure locale (GMT+2) avec mention :« REPONSE A L’AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DES MANIFESTATIONS D'INTERET BI-PAFEN-PIU-2.4.5.10-CS-INDV POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT CHARGE DE L’ASSURANCE QUALITÉ DANS LE CADRE DE L’ACQUISITION D’UNE PLATEFORME ELECTRONIQUE DE GESTION DES MARCHES PUBLICS ÉLECTRONIQUES (e-GP) AU BURUNDI »

11. L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence est la suivante :

Nom de l’Agence d’exécution : PAFEN

Adresse du bureau : Nouveau site du PAFEN à Bujumbura, Quartier Kinindo (Zeimet), jonction Rue Kiremba et Kinyinya, N°14 (Partie PAFEN), Tél :  +257 69 50 00 32 - Bujumbura - Burundi

Adresse électronique : procurement@pafen.gov.bi avec copie obligatoire à info@pafen.gov.bi, mvukiyekeges@gmail.com et nephtali.niyibizi@pafen.gov.bi

UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET

---------------------------------

 

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERÊTS N°057 /HISWACA /26

POUR LE RECRUTEMENT DE DIX- HUIT (18) ANALYSTES THEMATIQUES POUR APPUYER LES TRAVAUX D'ANALYSE DE L’ENQUETE DEMOGRAPHIQUE DE SANTE DU CONGO (EDSC-III)

 

1.Le Gouvernement de la République du Congo a reçu un financement additionnel de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA) pour la mise en œuvre des activités du « Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (HISWACA) », et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre des contrats suivants : « recrutement de dix-huit (18) analystes thématiques pour appuyer les travaux d'analyse de l'EDSC-III».

2.Objectif principal

L’objectif principal est de recruter et mobiliser des analystes thématiques qualifiés pour produire un rapport d'analyse de l'EDSC-III de haute qualité, conforme aux standards internationaux des enquêtes EDS et répondant aux besoins d'information des décideurs.

3.Objectifs spécifiques

De façon spécifique, il s’agit de : (i) renforcer les capacités opérationnelles et méthodologiques de l'équipe d'analyse à travers un atelier de cadrage ; (ii) harmoniser la compréhension des canevas de rédaction et des outils d'analyse entre tous les analystes ; (iii) assurer la production de chapitres thématiques de qualité dans les délais impartis ; (iv) garantir la cohérence analytique et rédactionnelle de l'ensemble du rapport final.

4.Profil des analystes

Les profils requis par groupe thématique et le nombre d’analyste sont présentés dans le tableau suivant :

Profil des analystes

Expert en échantillonnage et traitement DHS. Rôle de référent technique transversal, supervision qualité méthodologique.

procnotices.project_name: Regional Sahel Pastoralism Support Project II
procnotices.bid_description: Recrutement d'un consultant pour l'accompagnement technique des bénéficiaires des nouveaux sous-projets innovants de soutien aux chaines de valeur du bétail à l'élaboration des plans d'affaires  des sous-projets
procnotices.contact_address: Niamey
procnotices.contact_organization: REGIONAL SAHEL PASTORALISM SUPPORT PROJECT II - NIGER
procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIQUE DU NIGER

Fraternité-Travail-Progrès

MINISTERE DE L’AGRICULTURE ET DE L’ELEVAGE

PROJET REGIONAL D’APPUI AU PASTORALISME AU SAHEL (PRAPS) PHASE II

UNITE DE COORDINATION DE PROJET

 

 

Avis à Manifestation d’Intérêt pour le recrutement d’un consultant individuel pour l'accompagnement technique des bénéficiaires des nouveaux sous-projets innovants de soutien aux chaines de valeur du bétail à l'élaboration des plans d’affaires des sous-projets.

 

  1. CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATION DE LA MISSION

Le sous-secteur de l’élevage occupe une place importante dans l’économie nigérienne. Le cheptel national est estimé à plus de 50 millions de têtes toutes espèces confondues soit un peu plus 20 millions d’UBT, pour une valeur totale de plus de 4 000 milliards FCFA (DSE/MAG/EL, 2019).  Il emploie plus de 80% de la population active et 20% vivent exclusivement de l’élevage.

Bien qu’il ait bénéficié d’investissements conséquents, des efforts supplémentaires doivent être consentis pour réduire le déficit de production afin d’atteindre la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle.

L’enjeu majeur pour le Niger et la Banque mondiale est la promotion de l’élevage pastoral afin de rendre plus productif et compétitif, apte à contribuer de manière plus substantielle à la lutte contre la pauvreté, à l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, tout en gérant durablement ses ressources naturelles.

C’est dans ce contexte que le Gouvernement de la République du Niger et la Banque Mondiale ont réitéré depuis 2019, leur intérêt à poursuivre les efforts engagés depuis la Déclaration de Nouakchott en 2013 et convenir de la mise en œuvre de la 2ème phase du PRAPS, solidement ancré sur les fondements du PRAPS-1.

Le Projet d’Appui au Pastoralisme au Sahel phase II (PRAPS_II) est conçu pour contribuer à la recherche de solutions appropriées aux contraintes du secteur de l’élevage sur la base des principaux atouts et des leçons apprises des interventions antérieures.

L'objectif de développement du projet est « d'améliorer la résilience des pasteurs et des agropasteurs dans certaines zones ciblées de la région du Sahel ».

L’atteinte de cet objectif se fera à travers cinq (5) composantes techniques, adaptées pour prendre en compte d'autres domaines d'intérêt, jugés importants pour aborder de manière holistique quelques-uns des principaux facteurs affectant la résilience des populations pastorales et agropastorales. La zone d’intervention du projet couvre actuellement les huit (8) régions du pays.

Le PRAPS II sera mis en œuvre sur une période de six (6) ans à travers cinq (5) composantes que sont :

Composante 1 : Amélioration de la santé animale et contrôle des médicaments vétérinaires ;

Composante 2 : Gestion durable des paysages et amélioration de la gouvernance ;

Composante 3 : Amélioration des chaînes de valeur du bétail ;

Composante 4 : Amélioration de l'inclusion sociale et économique, femmes et jeunes ;

Composante 5 : Coordination du projet, renforcement institutionnel, prévention et réponse aux crises.

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de la composante 3 dont l’objectif général est « d’assurer l'accès des pasteurs et agropasteurs à des marchés concurrentiels et inclusifs et accroître le développement des chaines de valeur du bétail afin de favoriser la réduction de la pauvreté et renforcer la résilience des ménages dans les zones ciblées par le projet », il est prévu le Financement à Coûts Partagés (FCP) des sous projets de soutien aux chaines de valeur du bétail au profit des différents acteurs de la chaine.

La mise en place des FCP du PRAPS II est prise en charge par la sous composante 3.3 : Développement de la chaîne de valeur et financement de sous-projets. L'objectif de cette sous composante vise à faciliter l’accès au financement des activités innovantes des chaines de valeur du bétail.

Ainsi, pour assurer l’accompagnement des bénéficiaires pour la préparation, des sous-projets, le PRAPS-II-NE avait prévu le recrutement d’un Consultant Individuel pour aider les promoteurs à l’élaboration des sous projets et plans d'affaires innovants des initiatives de valorisation du bétail pastoral.

Les présents termes de référence sont préparés en vue de la sélection d’un consultant dans le cadre du financement à coût partagé du PRAPS II-NE.

 

II             OBJECTIFS ET RESULTATS ATENDUS

    1. OBJECTIFS 

L’objectif global de cette activité est de recruter un Consultant Individuel pour l’accompagnement technique des bénéficiaires à l’élaboration des sous projets et plans d'affaires innovants des initiatives de valorisation du bétail pastoral d’une part et d’autre part assurer le renforcement des capacités des porteurs de ces sous projets au niveau des Huit (8) régions du PRAPS.

De façon spécifique il s’agit de :

  • Aider le promoteur à saisir les opportunités, identifier les problèmes et les solutions possibles et faire un choix stratégique pour l’augmentation du niveau de rentabilité de son activité ;
  • Accompagner les bénéficiaires à l’élaboration des dossiers des sous projets et plans d'affaires innovants des initiatives de valorisation du bétail pastoral ;
  • Réaliser les différentes études complémentaires de base nécessaires pour l’élaboration et la finalisation du plan d’affaire des bénéficiaires retenus a l’issue de la sélection définitive (étude juridique, étude technique, étude commerciale, étude technique, étude financière) ;
  • Tenir les séances d’échanges sur les activités des promoteurs retenus pour comprendre ce qu’ils veulent faire et peuvent faire dans les trois (3)  a cinq (5) prochaines années pour développer leurs affaires (identifier les problèmes et les solutions stratégiques) ;
  • Faire la restitution du document du plan d’affaires au promoteur et apporter les corrections ;
  • Faire la restitution au PRAPS II du rapport d’élaboration de l’ensemble des plans d’affaire élaborés pour être soumis en vue du financement ;
  • Transmettre les plans d’affaires élaborer au PRAPS-2 NE.
    1. RÉSULTATS

Les résultats attendus de la prestation sont :

  • Le promoteur est aidé et à examiner les opportunités et surtout à identifier les problèmes et les solutions possibles en vue de l’augmentation du niveau de rentabilité de son activité ;
  • Les bénéficiaires sont accompagnés dans l’élaboration des dossiers des sous projets et plans d'affaires innovants des initiatives de valorisation du bétail pastoral ;
  • Les séances d’échanges sur les activités des promoteurs retenus pour comprendre ce qu’ils veulent et peuvent faire dans les trois (3) a cinq (5) prochaines années sont tenus et leurs affaires sont développées (identifier les problèmes et les solutions stratégiques) ;
  • Les examens complémentaires de base nécessaires pour l’élaboration et la finalisation du plan d’affaire des bénéficiaires retenus a l’issue de la sélection définitive (étude juridique, étude technique, étude commerciale, étude financière) sont réalisés ;
  • La restitution du document du plan d’affaires est faite au promoteur et des corrections sont apportées ;
  • La restitution des plans d’affaire élaborés est faite et ces plans d’affaire sont soumis en vue du financement éventuel ;
  • Les dossiers de demande de financements jusqu’à l’issue finale (obtention du financement ou rejet) sont suivis ;

III            PRODUITS (LIVRABLES)

Il est attendu du consultant, la fourniture des livrables ci-après :

  • Une note de cadrage, une approche méthodologique et un plan de travail finalisé ;
  • Un canevas d’élaboration des Business Plans sous format Powerpoint (PPT) ;
  • Les plans d’affaires préparés de façon participative ;
  • Les plans d’affaires sont restitués aux promoteurs ;
  • Les dossiers de demande de financements des promoteurs sont suivis ;
  • Un rapport global de la prestation en fin de mission.

IV.           PROFIL DU CONSULATANT

Le Consultant devra avoir l’expérience requise pour effectuer les services mentionnés ci-dessous. A cet égard, il doit avoir :

  •  Un diplôme de bac+5 en agroéconomie, économie ou équivalent
  • Un minimum de cinq (5) années d'expérience dans l'exécution de missions similaires ;
  • Au moins deux (02) références pertinentes dans l’élaboration de business plan des sous-projets innovant du domaine de l’élevage pastoral avec l’outil RuralInvest ;
  • Une expérience dans les analyses financières et économiques, et avoir déjà élaboré des business plans autour des chaines de valeur cibles du PRAPS II au profit des promoteurs des sous projets et avoir une expérience des mécanismes de Financement à Coûts Partagés serait un atout supplémentaire.

Le Consultant présentera ses principales références en matière d’élaboration des plans d’affaires, en précisant la nature des prestations similaires réalisées, les lieux, les zones géographiques, les délais, les dates de réalisation et les certificats de bonne exécution.

V. DUREE ET PERIODE

La durée de l’accompagnement technique est de 30 H/J étalés sur 3 mois.

VI.           ORIENTATION METHODOLOGIQUE

Le consultant proposera une orientation méthodologique dans le cadre de l’accompagnement des bénéficiaires à l’élaboration des sous projets de soutien aux chaines de valeur du bétail avec tous les outils d’appui conseil nécessaires (canevas des dossiers d’appel à proposition de sous-projet du PRAPS II, supports techniques, des études de marché, d’analyse financières, rapport d’étape etc) à cet accompagnement.

A cet effet, il proposera, dès le démarrage de la mission, une note technique d’exécution de la mission. Cette note fixera la démarche méthodologique, le plan et le chronogramme de réalisation des travaux, les moyens à mobiliser, les résultats attendus de la mission et les observations éventuelles sur les termes de référence de la mission.

VIII. METHODE DE SELECTION ET NATURE DU CONTRAT

Le/la consultant (e) sera sélectionné (e) selon la méthode « Consultant Individuel » avec comparaison de CV en conformité avec le Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI)” (Juillet 2016), révisé en septembre 2025.

L’évaluation et le choix du/de la consultant (e) seront faits sur la base d’une comparaison des expériences et qualifications au regard des exigences et de la nature de la mission selon une grille d’évaluation définie par le comité d’évaluation.

A l’issue de cette évaluation des CV, le/la consultant (e) le mieux classé sera retenu et appelé à négocier le contrat forfaitaire.

 

  1. DOSSIER DU CONSULTANT

Les dossiers de candidature, composés d’une lettre de motivation adressée à Monsieur le Coordonnateur National du PRAPS II, d’un CV à jour (faisant ressortir les expériences pertinentes du consultant pour la présente mission) et de la copie légalisée du diplôme exigé.

Les expériences similaires seront justifiées par des attestations de bonne fin.

 

Les Consultants intéressés peuvent déposer leurs candidatures à l’adresse ci-dessous en physique ou envoyés par email (format PDF) à l’adresse suivante  spm@praps2niger.ne avec copie à atteissa@gmail.com au plus tard le 31 Août 2026 à 17 H 00, heure locale de Niamey (TU+1) :

 

Unité de coordination du Projet Régional d'Appui au Pastoralisme au Sahel (PRAPS) Phase II Sis au quartier Village de la francophonie, Niamey Niger,

procnotices.notice_text:
Kano State Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project

PROJECT NO. P179684

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

IDA Credit No.: IDA-76370

 

Consultancy Services for the Preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for Jakara Irrigation Scheme Kano State

 

Reference No: NG-KANO STATE SPIN-553495-CS-CQS

 

Publication Date: August 17, 2026

 

The Kano State Government through the Federal Republic of Nigeria has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for payment of the Consultancy Services for the Preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for Jakara Irrigation Scheme Kano State.

 

The consulting services ("the Services") include conducting an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and preparing a Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for the rehabilitation of the Jakara Dam Irrigation Scheme. The Services include the preparation of the Inception, Draft, and Final ESIA and RAP Reports, including the Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), stakeholder consultations, and all other activities and deliverables specified in the Terms of Reference (ToRs), in accordance with applicable national regulations and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToRs) for the assignment can be found at the following link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-wvdML04cLXdiM-O4ED7wK_DX6Xdun50?usp=drive_link

The Kano State Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Proven experience as an Environmental and Social Management consulting firm in the preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), and Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) for irrigation, water resources, dam rehabilitation, agricultural, or similar infrastructure projects.
  2. Demonstrated working knowledge of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), particularly ESS1, ESS5, and ESS10, gained through hands-on experience in preparing and implementing environmental and social instruments for World Bank-financed or equivalent donor-funded projects.
  3. A minimum of eight (8) years' relevant experience in environmental and social assessment and resettlement planning for irrigation, water resources, dam rehabilitation, or similar infrastructure projects.
  4. Successful completion of at least three (3) similar ESIA and/or RAP assignments for World Bank-financed or other equivalent donor-funded projects.
  5. Demonstrated experience in environmental and social baseline studies, environmental and social impact assessment, stakeholder engagement, socio-economic surveys and census, asset inventory and valuation, livelihood restoration planning, biodiversity assessment, occupational health and safety, climate change assessment, gender and GBV/SEA/SH risk assessment, and preparation of Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs).
  6. Availability of adequate organizational and technical capacity, including access to a multidisciplinary team capable of undertaking assignments of similar scope and complexity.
  7. Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement, and report-writing skills.

Please note: The Qualifications and Experience of Key Experts shall not be included in the shortlisting criteria. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, Paragraphs 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Seventh Edition, September 2025), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

 

Interested Consulting Firms must be independent of and have no affiliation with any firm engaged in the design or construction of the Project.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

The consultancy services are expected to be completed within thirteen (13) weeks from the commencement date, during which the Consultant shall undertake the ESIA and RAP assignments concurrently in accordance with the Terms of Reference (ToRs).

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 8.00am to 4.00pm (local time).

 

Expressions of Interest must be delivered in writing to the address below, both in person and by e-mail, on or before Monday, August 31, 2026.

 

The State Project Coordinator,                       

Attn: Engr. Nuraddeen Isah Abubakar

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST - INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT

Resident Technical Assistant to support the Central Bank's Digital Transformation Agenda

Finance Agreement Reference: IDA-E0730

Project No. P177158

Assignment Title: Resident Technical Assistant to support the Central Bank's Digital Transformation Agenda

Reference No. 50/C/DSTP/2026

The Government of the Republic of Sao Tome and Principe (GoSTP) has received a grant from the World Bank toward the cost of the Digital São Tomé e Príncipe Project (DSTP) whose objective is to improve equity and sustainability of and to strengthen data governance, data systems and statistical capacity.

The Central Bank of São Tomé and Príncipe (BCSTP) recently acquired an ATS+ system—integrating three critical payment and clearing systems—to modernize its financial infrastructure. These systems are now in the implementation phase and constitute essential components of the national payment infrastructure. Their smooth operation is critical to the stability of the financial system and public confidence in payment systems.

The Central Bank requires a service provider (individual consultant) to deliver continuous, expert, and high-quality operational support to ensure the smooth functioning of RTGS, ACH, and IFT systems, guarantee service continuity, and progressively build the capabilities of BCTP’s internal teams toward autonomous and optimized operations.

The duration of the assignment will be for a period of 12 months renewable for an additional period of 6 to 12 months, depending on service requirements.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained by sending a request to the address email: digital.procurement@afap.st / cc daniel.vaz@afap.st.

DSTP invites qualified individual consulting (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the services sending a Letter of intent, Curriculum Vitae and proof of training and skills as stated in the Curriculum Vitae. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services according to the TOR.

Interested candidates should meet the following minimum requirements:

Education: University degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field.

Professional Experience: At least 5 years of professional experience in the operational support or management of critical payment systems, including ACH, RTGS and/or IFT.

Payment Systems Knowledge: Strong knowledge of payment system standards and processes, including RTGS/ACH/IFT, BCBS, CPMI and ISO 20022, as well as clearing and netting mechanisms.

Critical Operations and Incident Management: Proven experience in critical incident management, troubleshooting and rapid problem resolution, including experience providing 24/7 operational support and managing operational emergencies.

Financial Sector Experience: Sound knowledge of operational processes within central banks or major financial institutions.

Technical Skills: Knowledge of system administration, databases, monitoring and alerting tools, service continuity and disaster recovery, as well as information security standards and diagnostic/troubleshooting tools.

Languages: Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken.

Based on the requirements above, the evaluation criteria are as follows:

  • Required training and certification (20%);
  • Mandatory professional experience (35%);
  • Relevant technical skills (30%): RTGS/ACH/IFT, payment systems, technical infrastructure, tools and standards;
  • Behavioral and interpersonal skills (15%): Communication, teamwork, adaptability.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, i.e., from 08:00 17:00 hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to address below or in pdf format sent to the e-mail address below, by September 07, 2026, midnight (local time) and should mention “INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT TO PROVIDE the Technical Assistance to support the Central Bank's Digital Transformation Agenda”.

FSM Department of Resources & Development (FSM R&D), in collaboration with NORMA, State Fisheries/Marine Departments

Consultancy Services to Strengthen the Legal Frameworks for Coastal Fisheries Management in the Federated States of Micronesia

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION

The Government of the Federated States of Micronesia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program - Second Phase for Economic Resilience (PROPER) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) are for strengthening the management of coastal fisheries through review and gap analysis of legislative and regulatory frameworks governing coastal fisheries in the FSM states, and development of draft legislation and related recommendations, including areas relating to small boat registration and safety, community-based fisheries management, compliance, enforcement, stakeholder engagement, awareness and follow-on TORs.

The FSM Department of Resources & Development, with support from NORMA, and the State Fisheries/Marine Departments, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

1. Background and Context

FSM is an island nation in the western Pacific comprising Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei and Kosrae. Fisheries are a vital economic resource, and FSM’s coastal and near-shore resources are under state jurisdiction while offshore oceanic resources are retained as a national government function.

Under PROPER, FSM seeks to strengthen management of both oceanic and coastal fisheries and the critical habitats upon which they depend. The coastal component seeks to implement priority actions identified in the coastal fisheries situation analysis and related investment project profiles.

The TOR identifies that FSM lacks modern legal frameworks for coastal fisheries and that existing legislation is often not implemented or enforced. The assignment will support legislative assessment, consultation, and drafting of laws and regulations responsive to each state’s needs.

2. Assignment Objective

The objective of the assignment is to strengthen coastal fisheries management through review and gap analysis of the legal and regulatory frameworks governing coastal fisheries in the FSM states; development of draft legislation and related management recommendations; and broad stakeholder consultations across all four states, including municipalities, communities and outer island representatives where viable.

3. Scope of Services

The expected services will be delivered through the following stages:

Stage

Expected scope

Stage 1

Desk Review and Compilation of Laws and Policies

Stage 2

Legal Analysis and Gap Identification

Stage 3

Stakeholder Engagement and Site Selection - First Round

Stage 4

First Draft of Legislation and Management Recommendations

Stage 5

Stakeholder Engagement and Site Selection - Second Round

Stage 6

Second Draft of Legislation and Management Recommendations

Stage 7

Validation Workshop

Stage 8

Final Draft of Legislation with Workshop Feedback

Stage 9

Awareness Raising and Other Activities, including TORs for subsequent consultancies

Stage 10

Final Consultancy Report

The assignment is expected to require field work and consultations in all four FSM states, as well as desk-based legal and policy analysis, legislative drafting, reporting and support to stakeholder validation.

4. Expected Duration and Indicative Level of Effort

The total duration of the assignment is expected to be fourteen (14) months. The TOR indicates an expected total input of approximately twenty-five (25) person-months by key experts, working part-time across the assignment. The final team composition, level of effort and work plan will be proposed by the selected Consultant in its technical and financial proposals and confirmed during negotiations.

6. Required Consultant Profile and Experience

Interested consulting firms should demonstrate relevant experience and qualifications in the following areas:

  • Legal and regulatory review, gap analysis and legislative drafting for fisheries, marine resources, maritime safety, natural resources, environment or related sectors.
  • Coastal fisheries management, community-based fisheries management, compliance and enforcement, and sustainable fisheries policy, preferably in Pacific Island countries or small island developing states.
  • Experience supporting national and subnational/state government agencies with legal reform, stakeholder consultation and validation workshops.
  • Experience with small boat registration, vessel safety, minimum safety standards, licensing, compliance systems or related maritime/fisheries regulatory reforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage participatory consultation processes involving government, communities, municipalities, NGOs, outer island representatives and other stakeholders.
  • Experience preparing clear, practical reports, legislative drafting instructions, draft legal instruments, management recommendations, training/awareness TORs and final consolidated reports.
  • Demonstrated institutional capacity, project management systems and quality assurance procedures to deliver a 14-month multi-state assignment.

The indicative key expertise identified in the TOR includes Fisheries Legal Expert; Fisheries Management Specialist / Fisheries Policy and Development Planner; National Local Liaison / Community Facilitator; and National Legal Expert. Key experts and CVs should not be evaluated at the EOI shortlisting stage unless expressly required by the Bank-approved procurement documents; detailed staffing will be evaluated at the proposal stage.

7. Shortlisting Criteria

The Borrower will assess Expressions of Interest to determine the shortlist of qualified firms. The criteria below are proposed for use in the shortlisting assessment. The EOI evaluation should focus on the firm’s qualifications and experience, not on individual experts or detailed methodology.

Criterion

Indicative assessment considerations

Core business and years in business

Relevance of the firm’s core business to legal reform, fisheries/marine governance, natural resources, maritime safety, stakeholder consultation and policy/regulatory support; demonstrated operational history.

Relevant assignment experience

Similar assignments completed in legislative review, legal gap analysis, fisheries/coastal resource legal frameworks, community-based fisheries management, enforcement/compliance, maritime/small boat safety, and subnational legal drafting.

Technical and managerial capability

Firm’s capacity to manage a multi-disciplinary assignment across four FSM states over 14 months, including quality assurance, consultation logistics, reporting, legislative drafting, and coordination with government agencies.

Pacific / FSM / small island context experience

Experience working in Pacific Island countries, FSM, small island developing states, customary/community settings, outer island communities, and multi-jurisdictional state/national governance environments.

Team/partnership strength

Strength and relevance of team, JV, sub-consultant arrangements proposed to cover national legal systems, local liaison, community consultation and specialized technical expertise.

8. Selection Method and Next Step

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualification-Based Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers 7th Edition, September 2025. Under CQS, firms provide information on relevant experience and qualifications; the Borrower selects the firm with the best qualifications and relevant experience and invites that firm to submit technical and financial proposals for negotiations.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers 7th edition, September 2025, including provisions on conflict of interest, eligibility, fraud and corruption, and the Bank’s sanctions framework. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should clearly indicate whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if selected.
